text: Which library must be included to use dynamic memory allocation functions in C?
explanation: The <stdlib.h> library includes functions for dynamic memory allocation such as malloc(), calloc(), realloc(), and free().

text: Which function is used to allocate a block of memory dynamically?
explanation: All of the listed functions—malloc(), calloc(), and realloc()—are used for dynamic memory allocation. malloc() and realloc() allocate memory blocks, while calloc() additionally initializes the memory to zero.

text: What is the difference between malloc() and calloc()?

choices.label: A
choices.text: malloc() initializes memory to zero, while calloc() does not

choices.label: B
choices.text: calloc() allocates memory and initializes it to zero, while malloc() does not

choices.label: C
choices.text: malloc() allocates memory in multiples of two, while calloc() does not

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no difference between malloc() and calloc()

explanation: The key difference is that malloc() does not initialize memory, while calloc() allocates memory and sets it to zero.

text: What does the realloc() function do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allocates a new block of memory

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resizes an existing block of memory

explanation: The realloc() function is used to resize an already allocated block of memory, either increasing or decreasing its size.

text: What should you do after using malloc(), calloc(), or realloc() to avoid memory leaks?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the free() function to deallocate the memory

choices.label: D
choices.text: No action is needed; memory is automatically freed

explanation: After dynamically allocating memory, you should use the free() function to release the memory when it is no longer needed to prevent memory leaks.

text: What does malloc() return if it fails to allocate memory?
explanation: If malloc() fails to allocate memory, it returns NULL, signaling that memory allocation was unsuccessful.

text: Which of the following statements about dynamic memory allocation is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The size of dynamically allocated memory can only be increased, not decreased

choices.label: B
choices.text: Memory allocated with malloc() is automatically freed when the program exits

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dynamically allocated memory must be explicitly freed by the programmer

choices.label: D
choices.text: calloc() cannot allocate memory for arrays

explanation: Dynamically allocated memory must be explicitly freed using the free() function to avoid memory leaks.

text: What happens if you free the same pointer twice?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nothing happens; the second free is ignored

explanation: Freeing the same pointer twice causes undefined behavior, which may result in memory corruption or crashes.

text: What is a memory leak in C programming?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When a program accesses memory it doesn't own

choices.label: B
choices.text: When a program loses a reference to dynamically allocated memory without freeing it

choices.label: C
choices.text: When memory allocation fails due to insufficient memory

choices.label: D
choices.text: When a program uses memory that has already been freed

explanation: A memory leak occurs when a program loses a reference to dynamically allocated memory without freeing it, resulting in wasted memory.

text: Which of the following is a good practice when working with dynamic memory allocation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Always free allocated memory after use

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set pointers to NULL after freeing memory

choices.label: C
choices.text: Check for NULL before using a pointer

explanation: All of the listed options are good practices. Freeing memory, setting pointers to NULL after freeing, and checking for NULL before using a pointer are important steps to prevent memory leaks and undefined behavior.
